clue.text: Environmentalists such as Ethel Merman and Thomas Hardy?

definitions.text: Environmentalists such as Ethel Merman and Thomas Hardy?

parts.words: Environmentalists such as Ethel Merman and Thomas Hardy?
parts.note: each name holds a tree in its embrace: ethEL Merman wraps an elm, thomAS Hardy wraps an ash

explanation.surface: A singer and a novelist are oddly held up as green campaigners.
explanation.walkthrough: The names are not famous for ecology: the trick is that ELM spans 'Ethel Merman' and ASH spans 'Thomas Hardy', so each name literally hugs a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Eco-campaigners are mockingly called people who embrace forest trunks, a jokey idiom for green activists.

clue.text: Measure of stress that can be absorbed by three nestlings about to take flight at last

definitions.text: Measure of stress that can be absorbed

indicators.note: points to the final letter of the word flight
birds about to take flight scatter, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Three young birds in a nest are ready to fly off at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to take flight' shuffles THREE NESTLINGS together with the T that ends 'flight', signalled by 'at last'.
explanation.definitionFit: In engineering, this is the maximum pulling load a material withstands before breaking, a measure of resistance to stress.

clue.text: Right one, hiding in central point in nest

indicators.note: the pair of letters is tucked away inside the word for a centre

parts.note: the eye of a storm or target is its centre
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Something right lies concealed at the very heart of a nest.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle's or other raptor's high nest goes by this name, so a synonym.

clue.text: Ring in when dancing includes party dance

indicators.note: the jumbled word takes the party word inside it as well
the ring shape goes inside the jumbled letters
letters that dance move about into a new order

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A dance-caller rings in the moment when the party starts dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring in' and 'includes' are two separate insertions into the shuffled letters, which the check places to fit; 'dance' at the end is the definition, not more wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively American country folk gathering with square dancing, so an example of a dance.

clue.text: One getting in a pickle from using her Kindle

indicators.note: the answer is lifted straight out of the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: Someone gets flustered while trying to use an e-reader.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across usinG HER KINdle.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cucumber preserved in vinegar ends up, literally, in a pickle.

clue.text: Golfer circling edge of hole is …

indicators.note: the golfer's name goes round the edge word

parts.note: Ernie Els is a South African golfer
the lip is the rim of a golf hole
taken as written

explanation.surface: A golfer's ball rims the cup and the sentence trails off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the three-dot punctuation mark ending the clue itself, which also leads into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-dot punctuation mark showing an omission or trailing-off is named by this term.

clue.text: … in soft enough ground, accepting initially even the error exiting the trap?

indicators.note: the rim of the hole from the previous clue goes inside the word soft

parts.note: taken as written
the dots carry on from the previous clue, whose edge of hole is a lip

indicators.note: ground means crushed and reshaped, so these letters are mixed up
takes the opening letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Continuing the golf story: the ball sits in soft ground as a player tries to escape a bunker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' joins the first letters E and T, picked by 'initially', to ENOUGH before 'ground' mixes them. 'Trap' is a golf sand trap on the surface, but also slang for the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A verbal blunder is something wrong that escapes from one's mouth, here jokingly called the trap.

clue.text: Person who can't spell anoints new members of old sect

parts.note: in the Harry Potter books a muggle is someone with no magical powers, unable to cast spells

indicators.note: new signals the following word's letters made into something fresh

explanation.surface: Someone poor at spelling anoints recruits into an ancient sect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can't spell' means can't cast spells, not bad at orthography. The sect followed Lodowicke Muggleton in 17th-century England.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of the puritan prophet Lodowicke Muggleton formed a small English religious sect lasting from the 1650s.

clue.text: Breakfast item in pub's left one entering complaint: "Is hard to swallow"

indicators.note: the breakfast food goes inside the pub word

parts.note: a bar is a pub, here with its possessive giving the S
an egg is a typical breakfast food

indicators.note: the two letters go into the complaint word

parts.note: beef is slang for a grievance
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A diner moans that a breakfast item in a pub was impossible to get down.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for something incredible: a claim that strains credulity is one that cannot be accepted.

clue.text: Disconcert Arsenal without using wingers, gaining victory in Europe

indicators.note: the trimmed team adds the victory letters on the end
wingers are the outer players, so the end letters are dropped

parts.note: Arsenal Football Club are nicknamed the Gunners
VE Day marked Victory in Europe in 1945

explanation.surface: A football manager rattles Arsenal by playing without wide men yet winning in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club nicknamed the Gunners; 'wingers' are the first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw someone off balance or rattle their composure is a close synonym.

clue.text: Return of ice in one point three times as slippery?

indicators.note: the reversed word goes inside the run of compass points

parts.note: E (east) is a compass point, repeated three times

indicators.note: return means the following word is read backwards

parts.note: to ice someone is slang for to kill them

explanation.surface: Ice returns to a single spot three times, making it slippery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ice' is gangster slang for murder. 'one point three times' means the compass point East used thrice, with the turned word set inside after the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Being like an eel suggests being wriggly and hard to grip, so slippery, with the question mark flagging the stretch.

clue.text: Aid for tourists in Edinburgh's good online reading material

parts.note: guid is the Scots spelling of good, as said in Edinburgh
E is the prefix for electronic or online
a book is something to read

explanation.surface: An Edinburgh visitor's aid could be a well-reviewed online read.
explanation.definitionFit: A handbook for travellers describing sights and routes helps visitors find their way.

clue.text: Spike Milligan, finally covered in for good

indicators.note: the pair of words wraps around the picked letter

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

indicators.note: takes the closing letter of the comedian's name

explanation.surface: Comedian Spike Milligan, finally covered up for good.
explanation.walkthrough: Spike Milligan was a British comedian of the Goons; his first name is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tine of a fork or a pointed projection is a sharp spike.

clue.text: Weapon available from around threepence

indicators.note: the run of letters is turned the other way round
the answer can be taken out of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A weapon can be bought for a mere threepence.
explanation.walkthrough: THREEPENCE contains EEPE, and 'around' turns it backwards. Threepence was an old British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A fencing sword with a stiff blade is a kind of weapon.

clue.text: One making declaration in a counter-revolutionary fashion

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned about, so the letters are spun into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone declares something in a reactionary, counter-revolutionary way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter-revolutionary' looks like one political word, but 'counter' is fodder and 'revolutionary fashion' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pronounces or proclaims words clearly is declaring them.

clue.text: Liberal's surprisingly more gutsy

indicators.note: surprisingly signals the letters turning up in unexpected order

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician proves surprisingly brave.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for braver or more daring, from having more nerve.

clue.text: Strange I should tan poorly

indicators.note: done poorly means the letters come out muddled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pale person frets that they tan badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizarre or freakishly unusual, a synonym of strange.

clue.text: Removes tension from simmering feud, overseas area excepted

indicators.note: a simmering feud is stirred up, so its letters are mixed
excepted means the area letter is left out

parts.note: in a down clue, over means placed on top of, here before the word seas

explanation.surface: Calming a smouldering quarrel, with overseas territory excluded from talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is not a reversal: in a down clue it means the shuffled quarrel sits above the seas minus their area letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking the fuse from a bomb makes it safe, so figuratively calming a tense situation.

clue.text: Car horn very good in snow, oddly

indicators.note: the two words go inside the selected letters
takes the first and third letters of the word

parts.note: cor is the French word for a horn, as in cor anglais
pi is short for pious, very good

explanation.surface: Someone sounds a car horn in falling snow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Car horn' looks like one thing; 'Car' is the definition, a Ford model.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ford model of that name was a large executive saloon car.

clue.text: Body establishing English broadcasts, originally

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: The organisation set up to broadcast English programmes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the BBC, whose nickname this is, and its initial letters spell it.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname of the British Broadcasting Corporation, a public body for broadcasting.

clue.text: Desirable but unattainable ladies, mostly out to lunch

indicators.note: out to lunch means crazy, so the letters are scrambled
the last letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: Unattainable women, mostly away from the office at lunchtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfect in a way that exists only in imagination, so out of reach yet wanted.

clue.text: Before returning toilet roll to soft bit of furniture …

indicators.note: the anagram comes before the turned toilet word
rolling the words tumbles their letters about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: returning means the word is read backwards

parts.note: loo is a British word for a toilet

explanation.surface: A toilet roll gets placed on a soft item of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A low stool for resting the feet is a piece of furniture.

clue.text: Childless male, shortly to produce child

parts.note: SP abbreviates sine prole, Latin for without issue, used in genealogies

indicators.note: the name is cut short by its last letters

parts.note: Roger is a male name

explanation.surface: A man with no children is soon to become a father.
explanation.walkthrough: SP (sine prole) appears in family trees for someone who died childless.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a baby or small child.

clue.text: … heads for mugs of no-good drinks

parts.note: no plus G, the abbreviation for good
gins are drinks

explanation.surface: Fools down drinks of worthless liquor by the mugful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for mugs' adds that noggins are also small mugs or cups.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal slang for people's skulls or brains.

clue.text: Fairy ring finally seen where moon is nearest to us

definitions.text: where moon is nearest to us

parts.note: a peri is a fairy of Persian legend
the last letter of ring is G, written out as a word

explanation.surface: A fairy ring is at last spotted under moonlight.
explanation.walkthrough: The final letter of 'ring' is G, seen spelt out as GEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers name the orbital point closest to Earth with this term.

clue.text: Spooner's cursed pig will cheat

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: sworn as in sworn at, cursed
hog'll is a pig will

explanation.surface: A pig, cursed at, will cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of SWORN HOG'LL to get HORN SWOG'LL.
explanation.definitionFit: An American slang verb meaning to swindle or deceive.
